title: Treat modern CSS as adaptive material
principle: Argyle’s public teaching (Chrome/CSS advocacy lineage, nerdy.dev): lean on native CSS capabilities—container queries, cascade layers, color functions, scroll-driven affordances—so interfaces adapt instead of depending on JS-heavy approximations. Prompt AI to prefer platform CSS before libraries.
procedure: Ask: can container queries / :has / grid / color-mix solve this without JS?
Layer styles (reset → tokens → components → utilities) to control cascade fights.
Progressively enhance; keep a readable base without fancy features.
Document browser baselines honestly in the PR.
examplePrompts:
Rebuild this component with adaptive CSS (Argyle / modern CSS craft):
- Prefer container queries over window resize JS.
- Use color-mix / relative color where theming needs variants.
- Cascade layers to isolate resets vs components.
- Note progressive-enhancement fallback.
No endorsement of any tooling.
Delete the resize observer if a container query can express the same layout shift.
promptWhy: Pushes platform CSS before dependency creep.
tips: Pair with Open Props for tokens.
